Simulation-based calibration

Source: R/fp_sbc.R
fp_sbc.Rd

Checks that the sampler recovers the posterior correctly for a given design and set of priors (Talts et al. 2018; Modrák et al. 2025). Each replicate draws parameter values from the priors, simulates data with the design of data (as fp_prior_predictive() does), fits the model, and records the rank of the true value among the posterior draws. If the computation is correct, the ranks are uniform. Besides the parameters, it ranks the log-likelihood of the simulated data at the true values among its values at the posterior draws (log_lik), a test quantity that depends on the data and is sensitive to problems the parameter ranks can miss (Modrák et al. 2025).

Usage

fp_sbc(
  data,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  ver = ~1,
  markov = NULL,
  random_recorder = !is.null(data$recorder),
  random_fp = FALSE,
  random_det = FALSE,
  priors = fp_priors(),
  reps = 100,
  ndraws = 99,
  base_seed = 1L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  fit_args = list(chains = 4, parallel_chains = 1, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling =
    1000, adapt_delta = 0.95)
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_sbc'
plot(x, bins = 10, ...)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object that gives the design.

occ, det, fp, ver, markov, random_recorder, random_fp, random_det, priors

As in fp_occu(). The priors are both the ones the data are drawn from and the ones the model is fitted with, as the method requires.

reps

Number of replicates.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws, evenly thinned, among which the rank is computed; thinning reduces autocorrelation. It must not exceed the number of draws of each fit, and ndraws + 1 should be a multiple of the number of bins used by base::summary() and plot() (10 by default).

base_seed, parallel, fit_args

As in fp_calibrate().

x

An fp_sbc object.

bins

Number of histogram bins.

...

Unused.

Value

A data frame of class fp_sbc with one row per replicate and parameter: rep, parameter, truth, rank (0 to ndraws), divergences, and ok. base::summary() tests the uniformity of the ranks of each parameter, and plot() draws their histograms with the band expected under uniformity.

Details

This differs from fp_calibrate(): there, data come from fixed parameter values and the question is whether a model's intervals cover them, which tests the model against the data-generating process (including misspecification). Here, data come from the priors of the model itself, so the question is only whether the computation is right: a sampler problem, an error in the model code, or a prior that leads to extreme data shows up as ranks that are not uniform. A U-shaped histogram means posteriors that are too narrow; a hump, too wide; a slope, a bias.

Prior draws can produce extreme data (for instance, no detection at all); such replicates are fitted as they are, and their divergent transitions are recorded. The log_lik quantity is not computed with random_fp = TRUE or random_det = TRUE, whose site effects are not kept by the simulation. base::summary() uses a chi-squared test of the binned ranks, which is coarse; look at the histograms from plot() as well.

References

Talts, S., Betancourt, M., Simpson, D., Vehtari, A., & Gelman, A. (2018). Validating Bayesian inference algorithms with simulation-based calibration. arXiv:1804.06788.

Modrák, M., Moon, A. H., Kim, S., Bürkner, P., Huurre, N., Faltejsková, K., Gelman, A., & Vehtari, A. (2025). Simulation-based calibration checking for Bayesian computation: the choice of test quantities shapes sensitivity. Bayesian Analysis, 20, 461–488. doi:10.1214/23-BA1404

See also

fp_calibrate(), fp_prior_predictive()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 100, nocc = 10, seed = 1)
sbc <- fp_sbc(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ 1, random_recorder = FALSE,
              reps = 100, parallel = TRUE)
summary(sbc)
plot(sbc)
} # }
